survey: The object is a cowboy lasso shown flat against a purple background. It has three parts. (1) A coiled bundle of rope on the left, wrapped four or five times and bound at the top by a red tie whose two cut ends stick up. (2) A short tail that crosses the front of the coil at the bottom and hangs down, ending in a cream end cap. (3) A running strand that leaves the back of the coil at the lower right and passes through a cream honda (eyelet), forming a large oval noose on the right. The noose rope comes back into the honda, so the loop is closed. Both ends of the rope are accounted for: the capped tail and the noose at the honda. The coil's tie holds the wraps together. Nothing hangs loose or ends in mid-air, and the lasso could work: the noose can slide through the honda.

errors.where: Left side of the coil, its inner and outer wraps
errors.what: On the right side the coil shows four or five separate wraps, but on the left they merge into one thick, smooth tube, as if the turns melted together. That makes the coil read as a lumpy crescent instead of a neat stack of wraps.

fix: Coiled lasso rope with each wrap clearly separate and the same thickness all the way around the coil, including the left side; the turns sit side by side and do not merge into one thick tube.
